text: Model change, live Oct 26: each season now starts from the average of KenPom's and Barttorvik's preseason ratings (was KenPom alone). Backtest, spread plays 2.5+ vs the opener: November line value +1.09 to +1.29 (2015-17) and +0.83 to +0.87 (2024-26); totals unchanged.

Rule change, live Oct 26: for the first 7 days of each season, model totals are shifted so the day's average matches KenPom's scoring level. Before any games are played the model starts from last season's scoring, which put every 2026-27 total about 3.6 points below KenPom and the market. Two unders logged before the rule and not bet were voided (corrections below); two that were bet stand.

This channel posts every BET the model logs, at the time it is logged, whether or not it is bet, then its close, CLV and result. Posts are never edited; mistakes get a correction message. Bets logged before the channel opened are posted on its first day with their original logged time. The bet log is also timestamped with OpenTimestamps after every run (bets/bets.csv.ots in the repo).

Model frozen from Oct 26, 2026 until a Jan 15, 2027 checkpoint: no changes to the ratings, the projection, the betting rules or the cutoffs (spreads 2.5+, totals 3+, +2% EV at the price). Team ratings keep updating from every result, as the frozen code does. Any exception will be announced here the day it goes live. Frozen version: commit dfb4bc7 in the repo (MODEL_FREEZE.md lists file fingerprints).

Schedule note, recorded Oct 27: the card checks lines every 10 minutes around the clock. Overnight checks moved from every 30 minutes to every 10 minutes at midnight Oct 27, before the first games on Nov 1. No change to the ratings, the projection, the betting rules, the cutoffs or staking; plays may simply be alerted sooner after a line posts overnight. Recorded in MODEL_FREEZE.md.

Protocol note, recorded Oct 28: the season's final forward-test read moves from March 16 to Sunday, March 14 (Selection Sunday), after every game through that day is graded, so the verdict lands before the NCAA tournament starts. Same games (Nov 1 through Mar 14), same measures and thresholds; no game had been played. No change to the model, the betting rules or staking. Protocol v2.1, recorded in MODEL_FREEZE.md.

Record note, recorded Oct 28, before the first games: closing-line value (CLV) now has one definition everywhere, the forward test's primary close. For each sportsbook, its last fresh quote (no more than 5 minutes old) in the 15 minutes before tip; the close is the median across books. Result posts, the card, the record page, the weekly charts and the model-check alert all use it. A play with no fresh closing quote shows CLV as unavailable, with the reason, and is left out of averages; it is never counted as zero. Averages show how many decided plays have a close. The same-book CLV shown before is kept as a diagnostic only. No result had been posted yet, so nothing earlier changes. No change to the model, the plays, the betting rules or staking. CLV tracking is built, and will be marked verified only after it is checked on the first game. Recorded in MODEL_FREEZE.md.

Staking note, recorded Oct 28, before the first games: the stake cap (a market's stake held at half when its closing-line value averages below zero after 25 bets) now uses the same closing-line value the record shows, the median of each book's last fresh quote in the 15 minutes before tip. Bets without a fresh closing quote are left out and counted, so the cap waits for 25 bets that have one. The thresholds are unchanged and no current stake changes. No change to the model, the plays or the betting rules. Recorded in MODEL_FREEZE.md.

Logging note, recorded Oct 28, before the first games: when ESPN's start time and the odds feed's start time differ by 30 minutes or more, we now also log quotes in the 20 minutes before ESPN's start. The official closing-line value still uses the feed's start; a second closing-line value at ESPN's start is shown beside it, labeled as a diagnostic. This applies now to Memphis Over 152.5 at Iowa State (feed 6:00 pm ET, ESPN and the confirmed tip 7:00 pm ET). No change to the model, the plays, the stakes or grading. Recorded in MODEL_FREEZE.md.

Reporting note, recorded Oct 28, before the first games: closing-line value is now labeled "Alert CLV (points)". It measures the alert's number against the consensus close (the median of each book's last fresh quote in the 15 minutes before tip), not the price you got. Result posts now list each closing book's number and price beside it, and a close built from a single book is flagged as a one-book close. No change to the model, the plays, the stakes or grading. Recorded in MODEL_FREEZE.md.

New bet type, recorded Oct 29, before the first games: Band B. When the model's edge on a spread is 2 to 2.49 points (just under the 2.5-point cutoff) and the play still clears the +2% expected-value rule at the best price, it is posted as "BAND B (0.5u)" at half a unit, flat. Band B has its own record line and is never added to the main record, which stays exactly as it was: same model, same plays, same 1-unit stakes, same grading. Totals band B is switched off. The rule that decides whether band B stays (at 300 graded plays or March 14) is written in the forward-test protocol, Appendix B. Recorded in MODEL_FREEZE.md.

Data fix, recorded Oct 30, before the first games: when Barttorvik had not yet posted a day's ratings file, the card treated it as missing for good and used KenPom's number in its place. It now asks again hourly until the file appears, as the backtest assumed; KenPom's game-day predictions get the same rule. Replays of past days are unchanged, and each play's input stamp shows when KenPom stood in for Barttorvik.

Data note, recorded Oct 30, before the first games: Barttorvik's site refuses the servers the card runs on, so his daily ratings file is now fetched from our own computer and saved to the repo, where the card reads it. The model, its inputs and its rules are unchanged; until the first daily file arrives (expected around Nov 2), KenPom's number stands in, as each play's input stamp shows.

Correction and data fix, recorded Oct 30: Villanova +7.5 (Nov 1) came from a broken BetMGM quote in our odds feed (sign flipped, no price) and is void; it was never a real line. The card treated the missing price as -110, an assumption meant only for historical lines. Three guards now stop this: no price means no play; a book 3+ points away from the other books is skipped; an edge above 8 points (spreads) or 10 (totals) is flagged for review, never posted as a bet. Notre Dame-Villanova Under 149.5 is unaffected.

Rule fix, recorded Oct 31, before the first games: when several books are open, the card now takes a quote that qualifies as a play (2.5+ point edge and +2% expected value at that book's price) over one that only prices better without qualifying. Liberty at High Point had been held on the watch list although two books qualified (High Point -6.5 at -110); it is now a play. Every card run also re-checks every book and alerts if a qualifying quote is ever passed over.

Rule fix, Nov 1: once we hold a side of a game (spread or total), the card will never log the other side of that same market. On Notre Dame-Villanova the card logged Over 146 this morning while we already held Under 149.5 from Oct 25; that Over was voided (correction above) and the record counts the Under only. Picks, thresholds and staking are unchanged.

Rule change, Nov 2, before today's games: the card now logs a play only if it also qualifies against the game's opening line with the current model. A game that becomes a play only because the line moved away from us afterwards is no longer bet; it is tracked as research. In the backtest those line-move plays won 50.1% on spreads and 48.4% on totals in 2024-26, below break-even, while plays that qualified at the opener won 55.8-57.8%. The 38 line-move plays already posted (31 regular, 7 band B) stay as posted and are graded in their own line-move record, never mixed into the main record. Thresholds, the +2% EV rule, stakes, books and grading are unchanged.
Housekeeping for the opener rule, Nov 2: the research log of signals the rule stops is now saved on every run, and a game we already hold is not counted as one. No play, rule or record changes.

From Nov 2, this channel and the play alerts carry only main plays: each main play when logged, its result, and any correction. Band B plays and the line-move plays logged before the opener rule are still tracked and graded, in their own sections on the record page, but are no longer posted here, and none of them count in the official record.

Data note, Nov 2: Bart Torvik kindly whitelisted this model, so the card can read his daily T-Rank file again instead of falling back to the last file it had. Thanks, Bart. The model, its rules and the record are unchanged; this restores an input the model already uses.

Housekeeping, Nov 2: two fixes to the injury checker's bookkeeping. Its source-timing report had stopped writing after two pulls landed in the same second, and one check failed to save its log after sending an alert. Both are fixed. The injury source, alerts, picks and the record are unchanged.

Fix, Nov 2: at some neutral-site games the closing-line value was read from the wrong team's side of the spread (the odds feed and ESPN named different home teams). Two open plays showed a wrong CLV (Florida -5.5 now +1.0, was -12.0; Purdue +4.5 now -1.0, was +10.0). No graded play, posted result or the record changed.

Tracking note, Nov 2 (protocol v2.5): when ESPN's play-by-play shows a game tipped before the odds feed's listed start, the closing line now stops at the actual tip, so no in-play number can count as a close. Tip times are now checked while games are on, not only after. No graded play, posted result or the record changed.

Fix, Nov 2: ESPN switched which team it lists as home for Purdue-Gonzaga (neutral site) after Purdue +4.5 was logged. Plays are now graded by the team actually bet whatever the listing, and the card shows that play's current edge correctly (+1.0, not +8.0). No graded play or posted result changed.

Tracking note, Nov 3: closing-line value (CLV) is now verified. A first-game check recomputed the close from the raw sportsbook quotes and matched exactly, with every quote confirmed pregame against the actual tip. CLV is measured against the consensus close of 6+ books in the last 15 minutes before tip.

Tracking note, Nov 4: no change to how plays are picked, staked or alerted. From today each play also records the exact ratings and data tables it was built on, with their times, so any play can be rebuilt and audited later. We are also running a research-only test of whether waiting for the morning ratings update would do better than playing lines when they first post. It places nothing and posts nothing; it is read on Jan 15 and decided on Mar 14.

Rule note, Nov 4: if a data download fails and no valid copy of the data is available, that day's plays are held (not posted) until it loads, instead of being picked from incomplete data. Plays are never held just because a ratings update has not come out yet.
